text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Czech and Slovak Prime Ministers, Vaclav Klaus and Vladimir Meciar, are expected to meet in April.
- Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik believes Slovakia will be in the first group of post-communist countries to be integrated into the European Union.
- Most importers have not lowered prices despite the abolition of the import surcharge at the beginning of the year. So far the most significant decrease has been in prices of imported cars.

- Police have adjourned the case of an explosion in front of the house of the former member of the parliament Frantisek Gaulider, who quit the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) last autumn.
- The government holds its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda does not include any major economic items.

- The opposition parties which initiated a petition to call a referendum for direct presidential elections said they would ask Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic to call an extraordinary session to change the presidential electoral system by a constitutional law.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The state guarantees some 5.7 billion crowns in debt -- out of a total of seven billion crowns -- at troubled white goods producer Calex a.s..
- Czech Railways estimates Slovakia's losses caused by the recent strike of the Czech rail workers at 50 to 80 million crowns.
- The Slovak government will present the draft law on revitalisation of troubled businesses at the March parliamentary session.
PRAVDA - State-owned gas distributor Slovensky Plynarensky Priemysel (SPP) will take about 12 percent in the state-run arm industry coordinator DMD Holding.
SME - The Slovak secret SIS service has accused Czech public television of preparing a documentary aimed at discrediting the SIS. Czech television has rejected the charge.
